evidence.note: Validated val CE every 500 steps throughout the 9000-step run, reading each point against target and letting the trend justify continuing; established a continuous val trajectory rather than training blind.

Repeatedly flagged the script's rough 4-bytes/token bpb as biased, then computed accurate decoded-byte bpb (1.028) and used the 3-shift stabilized measure — proxy-noise-aware assessment vs the 0.983 target.
Detected the low-LR continuation plateauing (2.7558→2.7234 with shrinking gains), read it as 'far from the ~2.64 target,' and decided to switch strategies rather than grind fixed steps.
Tracked 12-layer vs 9-layer val CE at matched steps, saw it wasn't overtaking, and stopped/kept the 9-layer best — cross-run done-vs-remaining accounting.
Monitored big int4 model narrowing but never beating the 9-layer best, then interrupted and finalized the better checkpoint.
In n-gram phase tracked bpb precisely (0.998→0.9855→0.98245→0.98164) against 0.983, recognized near-threshold margin, and caught an off-by-one that had regressed bpb to 1.04.

reasoning: The agent sustained an accurate val_bpb-vs-target picture across many distinct runs (base, fine-tune, 12-layer, big-int4, n-gram), distinguished plateau from under-training, was explicitly aware the rough bpb proxy could mislead near threshold, and repeatedly reallocated effort based on that read rather than fixed step counts — matching the level-10 description. It falls just short of a perfect 10 because it let a couple of clearly-lagging runs continue through many validation points before stopping, so I place it at 9.
